title: MAViQ: Memory-Augmented Visual Querying for Multi-Turn MLLM Jailbreaks
reason: 核心贡献是利用跨轮反馈调整图文查询的交互框架，明确区别于固定图文对和仅文本的多轮方法。两个基准、六个目标模型的结果提供了量化基线比较，但摘要未报告消融，也未证明系统存储了图像记忆。
abstract: Jailbreaks against multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically operate through image-text inputs. After each target response, the attacker must decide how the new feedback should shape the next image-text query: which clues should be stated in the text, which should appear as visual evidence, and how the text should refer to the image.Existing multimodal attacks typically rely on fixed image-text pairs or candidate search, limiting their ability to adapt across turns.Text-only multi-turn attacks can adapt to prior responses, but they do not decide how response-derived clues should be expressed across image and text.In this paper, we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization} and propose \underline{M}emory-\underline{A}ugmented \underline{Vi}sual \underline{Q}uerying (MAViQ), a black-box framework that converts response-derived clues into visual and textual constraints, refines the query after observing the generated image, and propagates feedback to subsequent turns.Extensive experiments on two benchmarks across six target MLLMs show that MAViQ achieves average attack success rates (ASRs) of 70.60% on MM-SafetyBench and 82.13% on JailbreakV-mini, outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively. Our code is available at  https://github.com/jixingtian/Maviq.
evidence: we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization}
result: outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively.
